summary: The profiled integer-fill kernel is limited by DRAM write bandwidth; these metrics do not characterize the supplied attention kernel.
reasoning: DRAM throughput reaches 83.13% (467.7 GB/s), versus 4.32% SM throughput. Active-warp occupancy is 87.71%, supporting a bandwidth bottleneck rather than insufficient occupancy. The reported kernel is at::FillFunctor<int>, not _flash_attention_kernel.

root_causes.cause: Bulk initialization stores dominate measured memory traffic.

evidence.interpretation: Writes account for approximately 97.9% of the measured DRAM bytes.
The write-heavy operation already uses most sustained DRAM bandwidth.

fixes.fix: Locate the integer-fill allocation in the profiled workload and eliminate its initialization if every element is overwritten before being read.
fixes.rationale: Removing unnecessary stores reduces the dominant traffic directly; verify complete overwrite before changing initialization.

root_causes.cause: A standalone fill pass performs little computation per byte transferred.

evidence.interpretation: Compute utilization is low while DRAM throughput is high, consistent with the reported fill operation.
High active-warp occupancy makes insufficient occupancy an unlikely primary limitation.

fixes.fix: If initialization is required, fuse it into the kernel that first uses the buffer where synchronization and semantics permit.
fixes.rationale: Fusion can avoid a separate initialization pass and intermediate traffic. Profile _flash_attention_kernel separately before applying attention-specific tuning.
